lines.text: Previously on "Gilmore Girls..."
This is an important family. Marrying into it is important business.
A girl like Rory has no idea what it takes to be in this family, Logan. She wasn't bred for it.
I don't understand.
They treated her like trash.
I highly doubt that.
I have an internship available if you're interested.
There is something wrong with this internship.
My God, you're paranoid.
It's tough business.
Definitely.
You don't got it.
Rory's quitting Yale.
What?
I thought between the three of us we could knock some sense into her but I really need the two of you to back me up on this.
Of course we'll back you up.
Rory will be taking some time off from Yale. She will be moving into the pool house here with us.
Have you talked to Rory about this? Your great plan?
She told me what she wanted in her own words.
Oh! Winded. Too many steps.
I said I'd carry em'.
Need water. Gunga Din!
They're not that heavy.
Yeah, you should take those steps out. They get in the way.
First thing tomorrow. Man, you bought a lot of stuff.
All stuff I need or want or think I might someday need or want. Okay, well, let's find your new wallet.
Oh, we can get it later.
No, it's buried in here somewhere. Have I looked in this bag already?
You didn't have to buy me a new wallet. My old wallet was fine.
Your old wallet has Velcro.
It works.
It's disgusting. Come on, let's find it. Wait a second. What is this?
Your underwear.
Oh, thanks a lot.
I didn't see how big they were. What are they doing in there?
Well, I'm guessing, probably hiding from their real owners, 'cause I would hate to be wrapped around the woman who fit those.
No, you just grabbed the wrong bag.
Oh, poor thing, she's single.
It still applies.
Hello? Sookie, Sookie slow down. I can't understand a word you're saying.
She's got huge feet.
The inn's on fire?
What?
Oh, the stove is on fire? Well, put it out. It's out? So, you're saying there was a fire but now it's out. Good, what's the damage?
You had a fire?
Okay, okay, good. I'll be right there. The wall behind the stove have caught fire. There's damage but nothing major. Thank God.
Come on. I'll take you.
Oh, my God, another fire at the inn like the Independence Inn. Oh no. Am I a fire starter? I'm a fire starter, aren't I?
You are not a fire starter. Caesar, we'll be right back.
What about the bags?
Caesar will put the bags away. Let's go.
No, go first. In case things burst into flames behind me as I walk.
Will do.
I saw my whole life pass before my eyes that's how traumatic it was!
She's been Scarlett O'Hara for two hours. It's sickening.
My whole life, flash. I mean, that's upsetting! You know, not that it's been a bad life although I could have skipped seeing "Mummenschanz."
Do you want to hand me the screwdriver?
I would kinda need a third hand to do that.
Why are the boy's bickering?
There's something in the air today.
Could you not shine that in my face?
Just move your face.
You mean off of my head?
So, Mutt and Jeff, what's the prognosis there?
When's the last time you checked your ductwork?
Never. Oh, boy, I shouldn't be allowed in a kitchen.
My guess is that the grease built up in the back and ventilation's not great, the wall heated up and burned.
So what do we do?
Don't tell me we're shut down.
You have to repair the wall before you put the stove back and you're gonna have to clean your ductwork. Which means closing the kitchen till you do.
Well, then, fix it now.
You need a pro to do this.
And if an insurance guy doesn't see it before you fix it, he won't pay.
Well, I've already talked to the insurance company. They've never heard of us.
That's impossible, we're customers. We send them a check every month.
The people I talked to, all very rude by the way, they said they don't even cover businesses such as ours.
Again a mistake. I'll get the policy out. I'll call them myself. Thank you.
You really should get a second screwdriver.
Nag, nag, nag.
We should be flayed.
Don't overreact, Nora.
We should never have let it get to this point. We're all at fault here.
We'll be the laughingstock of the DAR. We'll lose our national accreditation and this is a very weak drink.
It's just punch, Nora.
My point, dear.
We've insulted the organization insulted our troops. We might as well all march to Mount Vernon, drop our drawers and do something foul on George Washington's grave.
Nora!
I'm sorry. But I'm really upset about this and I'm far too sober to put it in any sort of perspective.
But the function is still a week away. There's time to fix this.
She's new, ladies.
A week is nothing.
Again, what do we do?
Is it definitely too late to do something?
To do what?
I don't know. To publicize the event more, get those tables sold?
We spent our budget for publicity. We're wiped out.
But a budget is just an estimation. It's guesswork. Fake numbers. In any business endeavor sometimes it makes sense to run a deficit in order to achieve a bigger payoff later.
We're lunching with Grover Norquist.
Well, have we tried getting the word out online? A lot can be done that way. And maybe we could add some entertainment or a theme, send out some e-mails. E-mailing doesn't cost a thing.
We hadn't thought about e-mail.
I think there's a way to correct this. A week is plenty of time.
Well, well, well, we have a star amongst us.
You.
Me?
Take it over.
What?
I don't know. We have a mountain here, ladies.

We're screwing the pooch, Emily and we've got to go balls out. I, for one, will not have those priggish twigs from the New York chapters lording this over us. We need to take a swing here and Babe Ruth sits before us.
You shouldn't feel pressured.
I know.
My essence is that if Rory doesn't think she can do it, she'll turn us down.
I suppose that's true.
What do you say, slugger?
I'll do it.
Yes! Let's ring Constance.
I'll set up a discretionary fund. This publicity idea you were thinking of may be the key.
Dig in, everybody.
I'm past digging, I'm burrowing. This is delicious.
Tri-tip on the barbecue, you can't beat it. Oh! Hey, you turn the barbecue off?
The barbecue is off. Good stuff, huh?
Really good.
Thanks. Excuse me. Davey, turn the volume down!
The vegetables are good, Sookie.
Thanks, Luke. Davey, you heard your father. Turn it down!
Oh, I'll turn it down.
No, we want Davey to do it.
That's how he learns. You heard me, son. Turn it down.
Turn it down!
Right now.
Ooh, I need a lemon slice.
So, did anybody see that new show on TV last night?
The one where they were solving crimes by cutting bodies open and poking their organs?
No.
The one where they're solving crimes from 30 years ago by going to graveyards and cutting open bodies and poking their organs?
No.
Oh.
The one where people are missing and then they find their bodies and cut them open, and poke their organs and that's how they solve crimes?
No.
What else is on?
You gotta turn the TV down, son!
Are you sure you don't want me to--
He's got to learn. You heard me, son! Volume down!
Volume down!
Listen to your mother.
Now, what's that show I'm thinking of?
I'm back. You like the squash, Luke?
Oh, this is gonna bug me. I'm not a big fan of the squash.
Oh, I forgot the pepper flakes.
Sookie, your food's getting cold.
I thought you liked squash.
Nope.
What's that vegetable I thought you liked?
Hey, Sookie, do you have a fork for Paul Anka? He likes his own fork. Plastic preferred.
Got one here.
Oh, now, this is gonna bug me. What is that vegetable?
The plastic's too high for me to reach. It's up there.
Oh, I'll get it. You have to eat.
Jackson, what's that smell?
Oh, man, I left the barbecue on.
We cannot set this place on fire too. I have had enough fires this week.
I'll get it. Turn the volume down, Davey. I'm not gonna tell you twice.
Here you go. It's nice and lean, the way you like it.
Dog who doesn't like fat is just weird.
He's not weird. He's trying to maintain bathing-suit figure.
So, speaking of my least favorite word in the world, fire where are we with the insurance company?
Ah, nowhere. I got the same run-around they gave Michel.
Then let's just do the work. Forget the insurance. Give me back my kitchen.
Tom's all ready to jump in but we can't afford to do it without the insurance money. That's why we have insurance.
We have stupid insurance. I mean, this policy, wasn't it set up by your--
Yes.
If we're getting the run-around does it mean that you have to...
Yes.
Sorry.
I know, it seemed like a good idea at the time. I'll call him tomorrow.
Barbecue's off.
Martha's up.
I'm on it. Turn the TV down, Davey.
Turn it down. You heard us, turn it down. I-I'm gonna count to ten, Davey then the TV is going off for the rest of the week. Ten. Nine. Eight. Seven. Six. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
She threw out the menu.
Hmm?
Rory, she's changed the entire menu.
What menu?
Richard, listen when I talk to you.
I'm sorry, Emily. Takes a second to emerge from Samuel Beckett. He's a strange man. Go on.

Rory threw out the entire menu for the Fort Drum event. I mean, granted, Constance was going with Cornish game hen, been there, done that and her fetish for Brussels sprouts is upsetting. But to throw out the entire menu? So close to the event?
I can't say that I'm a big fan of DAR cuisine so, I may not be of much help.
I'm trying not to butt in but how can I not worry?
By not thinking about it.
Is there still a USO?
I think so. Why?
That's the theme, the USO. Or that's where it's being held. Oh, my God, she didn't change the menu and the location? Is that possible?
You should ask her.
I'm trying to keep out of it.
You're doing a terrific job.
She's not serving salmon puffs.
Good night, Mr. Beckett.
We've never not served salmon puffs. Not in 25 years have we staged an event without salmon puffs.

Emily, please. It's Rory. What she tackles, she conquers. This girl could name the state capitals at three recite the periodic table at four discuss Schopenhauer's influence on Nietzsche when she was ten. She's read every book by every author with a Russian surname and had a 4.2 grade-point average at one of the toughest schools on the East Coast. If she's excluding salmon puffs she has a good reason to exclude salmon puffs. And I, for one, have complete confidence in her ability to tackle this job and so should you.
Fine, go back to your Beckett.
Thank you.
Salmon puffs.

We'll show 'em, huh, guys? We'll show 'em you don't need fancy stuff like stoves in order to make a delicious meal. We've got salads, lots and lots of salads caprese and endive and arugula and, ooh cold sandwiches and beef carpaccio and tuna carpaccio and vegetable carpaccio. Oh, my God. Am I ever gonna get the stove back? I'm dying here!
Okay. Hang in there, hon. Thanks.
Lorelai, I hope it's alright walking in like this. I knew where the kitchen was so, I just figured I'd come back. Sookie.
You're our knight in shining armor, Mr. Gilmore.

This is Harris, he'll do the inspection get the lay of the land. Shouldn't take long. Go ahead and start. I should apologize for the red tape and the delay. As a rule, we don't take on small accounts like this except under extraordinary circumstances. Until the news reached my desk, no one was sure of what to do.
Uh-huh.
I can write you a check today. I figured that would please you.
Terrific.
I'm gonna go call Tom and see if he can race right over here and start the work. Bless you, sir. You're my golden God.
So, um... how's your big plan working out?
Excuse me?
Oh, your big plan for Rory. How's that going, dad?
Let me know if you need anything, Harris.
Is she back at Yale?
Lorelai--
Oh, I take it she's not.
No, she's not.
Huh! But it's in the works.
We'll be here ten minutes.

No, wait let me guess you're gonna trick her into going back, right? Like you'll drive up and drop her off at Yale and then you'll drive away really quickly before she catches on. Is that one of the plans?
Is there anything I can do to expedite this, Harris?
You see that family of Logan's recently The... Hamburgers?
Huntzbergers.
Right, right. How are the old Huntzbergers? They behaving any better than that night they humiliated your granddaughter?
They did not humiliate her.
Rory said they did.
I know the Huntzbergers. They're fine people. What happened that night was a misunderstanding because they have nothing against Rory.
No?
Why would they?
Ask them!
It's not true.
Well then that granddaughter of yours, what a liar.
Harris, take a couple of pictures and we'll go. We just need the quote from your contractor in writing. Send all his bills directly to me.
Will do.
Goodbye.
It's been lovely.
What about silverware?
I can get you 1940s. They're real thing. It's plates though. Plates are a toughie.
Plates break.
I can get you a couple of dozen hand-painted, not a 100.
So, what's our best bet, an off-white, new but made to look vintage?
Off-white would be super.
And they should be heavy, right, solid?
Oh, my servers are gonna love that.
Then not too heavy. Lacey, get me samples of all this?
Will do.
Now, there must be a color photo of the Hollywood Canteen. I mean...
We've checked the internet. The library? The Getty in California has one in their collection but they're very flaky on the phone.
Oh, California.
I'm so over the West Coast.
A bunch of granola heads.
Rory Gilmore's phone. Who's calling? One moment, please. It's Logan Huntzberger.
I'll take that. Hello?
Oh, my God. Who was that?
My assistant. I forwarded my phone to hers.
You have an assistant?
Just for this DAR Thing. I get a million calls.
I consider myself lucky to be patched through.
You have priority clearance.
So, good news, I got the PA system you wanted at the price you wanted.
Really? Oh, cool. Lacey, PA system, done.
Excellent.
That's great. This guy's done the sound at every party I've ever thrown. He's the best in the business.
And oh, goody. Paris is here. And she looks upset.
That and a bulldozer would knock me over.
Excuse me? The door is locked.
Do you know her?
Let her in, then hide. I'll call you later.
Bye.
"Do you know her?" I'm only her best friend. Who the hell are you?
Paris, come here. Calm down. What's wrong?
I'm broke.
Broke? How?

My parents flipped the bird at the IRS. One too many times. They've frozen everything. All I've got is my trust fund which doesn't kick in till I'm 25. So, unless you can whip out a magic wand and age me four years, I'm a goner.
Just sit down. Calm down.

My ATM refused me. I thought it was just that particular one. So, I went to another and it refused me too. So, I went to the bank and used a few choice expletives and a bunch of guys in suits started closing in on me. So, I started pacing and yelling, "Attica! Attica!" Then the manager hit a little red button under his desk so, I ran out of there and came right over here. I'm a pauper. I'll be playing a hurdy gurdy on street corners. And selling pencils out of a tin cup.
Slow down.
Yale's paid for... Through the end of the year, thank God. But what'll I do about everything else I need? What will I do?
You'll just have to do what everyone else who needs money has to do.
What's that?
What people do.
What am I, a mind reader?
Get a job.

A job? I've never had a job. I don't know the first thing about having a job. All I've got on my resume is academic achievements which will mean doodly-squat when I'm in line with 11, 000 people vying for an opening in the garden department at Walmart.
Paris, wait. As you said, Yale's paid for. That's the bright side. From now on, you'll just have to keep your expenses low. And I could get you some work? Right away. How would that be?
Really?
Yes. I know you'll be a hard worker. That's a given.
I definitely would be. And you know, I speak Chinese and Farsi. If that'll help.
I need servers for the food. You could do that, right?
I think so.
See? You're on the road to recovery.
Oh, thanks.
And I'll work my butt off too, Glenda. Oh, and I know a smattering of ancient Aramaic, if that helps.
It could.
If Christ shows up.
And who are you?
Go home, Paris. You've had a rough day.
I guess.
I'll call you with the details.
Thanks. Hey, uh, can you spot me a 20?
Sure.
Oh, here you go.
Thanks.
I owe you more than you currently realize. Okay, where were we?
Pasta's almost done, sauce is close too.
You know, we could've just used the store-bought sauce I have.
Oh That stuff is junk.
Oh, it's delicious Italian sauce.
Okay, first off, it's not. Second, all you had was four already-opened jars two of which I couldn't get the lids off of.
Somebody needs some gym time.
And one of them had a layer of white fuzz on it.
That was a little gross.
And the last one, green fuzz.
Also gross.
I make better. Just like mama taught me.
I know you do. How's Paul Anka's dinner coming?
His hamburger's close too.
You're not overcooking it, 'cause you know he likes it rare plus, you know not too rare, but not medium rare.
I'm cooking it to his exacting specifications. Miss Patty's having a recital?
Oh, yeah. It's her big annual show. All her kids in all her classes get to perform. It's be there or be square, best show in town.
This Thursday, right? It's a good night. I'll have Caesar close for me.
Why?
So I can go with you.
Oh, no. Luke, you're not going to this recital.
Why not?
Because it's a night of kids dancing singing, twirling batons, you'll hate it.
No, I won't.
Yes, you will.
It's not my first choice in entertainment, but I'll go.

Luke, no, you have been sacrificing too much of yourself these past few months. You go with me to my movies. You tag along when I go shopping. And that dinner at Sookie and Jackson's, how you kept from killing us all, I'll never know.
I haven't been complaining about any of this.
I know, and that has filled me with no end of guilt. You've been a saint, but you've gotta do your Luke stuff too. When was the last time you went camping or fishing?
You don't like camping or fishing.
That shouldn't stop you from camping or fishing.
I'd go if I felt like it.
Well, then go Thursday while I'm at the recital. I'll go with Sookie. It'll be fun with her.
You sure?
Yeah, go. You haven't been camping in forever. Be "Grizzly Adams."
Okay sure, I'll go camping.
Good. Oh, that's officially it.
Oh, medium rare, not rare plus. I'll get him another.

I don't know why I had bothered. The great books take practically a lifetime to read as it is. But if you heed the word of Mortimer Adler "One needs to read a classic three times to fully comprehend its meaning."
Yeah.
I wonder if Mortimer ever read "Euclid's Geometry" three times. That's a fun read. Have you read "Euclid's Geometry"?
Me? No.
It doesn't get any drier. What have you been reading lately? I keep forgetting to ask.
Rory?
Sorry, guys. The event's right around the corner and I just keep thinking of things I have to do. I'm just texting Lacey.
So how's that going?
Good, really good.
Good. Did Lacey mention partitions?
Partitions?
At Waff ord Hall. It's so big, and these partitions can cut the room wherever you like, so, it won't look so empty. They're not very decorative, but they work.
Oh. Hold on just a second. Partitions?
For the room.
But we won't have any room, we're sold out.
Sold out? That's not possible.

Oh, it's a fact. The theme got people's attention. Plus, the online campaign went like gangbusters. We're having to turn people away. That's what I was texting Lacey about. I'm trying to squeeze in a few more but we're fighting the fire department over it.
You're turning people away?
But still encouraging them to give a sizable donation to our boys.
Brilliant!
Sold out!
I knew you could do it.
Good job!
Thank you.
Continue texting.
Oh, thank you.
Oh, when the band gets here, grab Jerry and get them to do a sound check, make sure they're happy with the sound. Not just Jerry, because... Lacey? Where's my Lacey?
Here.
Come on, honey, keep up.
I spotted the security guard, so I filled him in.
Excellent. Cross that off the list. Servers are here?
Got them all waiting in the back.
Excellent. Whoa. Treat her gently there, boys. Betty's life was tough enough.
Hey, Paris.
Rory, I clocked in.
Cool.
They gave me this card. And it had my name on it. I shoved it in the clock thing and it made the punchy sound and I'm officially on the job.
Great!

And I'm prepared too. I was a little nervous last night about making small talk with co-workers so, I went to the video store and rented "Working Girl" and the first season of "Just Shoot Me." Got a couple of Wendie Malick bon mots that have already come in handy.
Very good. Welcome.
Thanks, boss.
I'm gonna welcome the whole group here.
No problem.
Hello. You must be my servers. I'm Rory Gilmore. I'm running this little shindig. How are all of you today?
You all come highly recommended by Glenda, our catering manager so I know you're all top notch.
Yeah, super. Looks like a good group. Good group.
Um, you know, um, you should probably be standing over with the others.
Oh, right. I'm one of them. Got it. Sorry.

So, it's going to be hard work tonight. We have a 100 people dining with us. But I want you to have fun too. We have your outfits on a rack over here. Your name should be on them. It's a good cause so let's get changed and go do.
So, working hard or hardly working?
Hey. Thank you. So, where's Luke tonight?
As we speak, he's off communing with nature.
Oh, good for him.
Yeah.
Ooh, the ballerinas are doing "Swan Lake." That always makes me cry.
Oh, Patty's packed it all in. "Baton twirling, a modeling exhibition."
She's added a couple new features too.
Yeah, what's krumping?
Um, like hip-hop dance, I think, more herky-jerky.
And what is pubic speaking?
I'm hoping it's a misprint.
I hope so too.
Welcome, everybody to the 28th Annual Miss Patty's school grand recital.
Thank you. We have a lot on the program tonight. So, without further ado please welcome my intermediate pupils as they welcome you. Hit it, boys.
She always does a fun opening number.
People seem hungry tonight. Tell--
Glenda to speed the trays up a bit.
Yeah, and let the sound guy know--
That the drums are a little loud.
And it's a tad warm.
Already had them adjust the AC.
Any incoming choppers, radar?
Choppers? No. What do you mean?
Oh, that was a joke, Lacey.
Oh. Sorry.
You're a doll. Remember to have a little fun tonight too.
Radar I get it now. That was funny. I'll be back.
Appetizers?
Thank you. We're the Gilmores.
Richard, look at this place!
It's wonderful.
Oh, thank you.
Yes, thank you. Oh, I love this song. And look at the band! It's the Andrew's Sisters.
They've kept in pretty good shape.
Hi, guys.
Looks like you've got a hit on your hands.
So far, so good. No one's dancing, though.
It's early. You'll see plenty of dancing after dinner.
You'll see some dancing right now.
Richard, it's before dinner. There's no dancing during appetizers.
Come on, let's show these fuddy-duddies how it's done.
My father was a huge Benny Goodman fan. Hated Glenn Miller, hated him. Always claimed it wasn't the enemy who shot down that plane of his, but music lovers.
Oh, Richard, that's a horrible thing to say.
It was my father who said it.
But you just repeated it. Here's the woman of the hour.
Ah!
How's the food, everybody?
The macaroni and cheese, what an inspiration!
Rory, please accept my profound thanks for serving food at a DAR event which is remarkably edible.
Oh, Richard. We always have good food.
Well, you have fancy good food. If I never look at another duck's liver for the rest of my life, I will be a happy man.
Rory, could I pull you away for just a second?
Sure. Excuse me, everybody.
She's so poised... ...like you, Emily.
A party's arrived. I'm looking, looking. They did not RSVP. But they're expecting a table.
Oh, great! Where are they?
By the war bonds table. It's Shira Huntzberger. She waltzed in with a group of ladies in tow and made it very clear that she expected to be accommodated.
Did she?
And not very nicely either.
Oh, what a shock.
But you know her, right? She's your boyfriend's mother.
Yeah, yeah. I know her.
I didn't mean to insult her. She was just very abrupt.
It's okay. I'll take care.
Here's the seating chart.
Thanks.

Hey, boss. It's interesting, you know. Karl Marx has come alive for me today. I never understood what he was yammering about before. And now, it just seems so obviously wrong that those who control capital should make their fortunes off the labor of the working class. What's wrong with you?
Shira Huntzberger is here.
Logan's mom?
And she showed up with no warning, no RSVP no donation to the cause that I know of. Just sashayed in, expecting everyone to fall at her feet.
I hate that.
I hate her. Hate, strong, unadulterated, blind, ah!
Wow. You're always so Desmond Tutuey. This is refreshing.
I should tell her to leave. I should march up to her and tell her to grab those arrogance-dripping petulance-oozing surgically cosmeticized bims she brought along and hit the bricks.
I bet they all have money too. Every one of those commodity fetishists.
How can she expect a table? The tables are for the people who are polite enough to respond to an invitation in the proper manner.
I bet you the Romanovs never RSVP'd either. They got theirs. Capitalist scum.
I hate her.
I hate the rich. A hard rain is gonna fall, you know what I'm saying?
I really hate her!
They should die.
I should probably give her a table.
What?
Well, we have a spare table. We kept it open in case of something like this. I should give it to her.
But she doesn't deserve it.
I know, but this is business. It's not personal. I should give her that table.
Fine. Whatever you think. You're the boss. Hey, boss, how much are you being paid in this job of yours?
Mrs. Huntzberger.
Rory, hi! What are you doing here?
I'm running this event.
I didn't know.
Well, now you do.
I think I've been bad.
Oh, really? Why?
I just showed up without any warning. I didn't think I could come, so I didn't call. Then I could, and the group and I just came down.
It happens.
That's what I told that other girl. She was a bit rude.
Lacey? I'll talk to her.
Could you get us a table?
Of course.
It's not a problem?
Oh. Not at all. Come with me. It's all set up.
Oh! You are the best.
It's just my job.
So, no Logan?
Not tonight.
Not his thing?
Oh, you know Logan. Here we are.
Thank you so much. And you look so pretty.
So do you. Have a good time.
I'm sure we will.
You've created a superstar here tonight, Emily. I hope you know that.
Well, yes, I do.
There's already talk of giving her the AA.
An AA?
An Abigail Adams... For distinguished service above and beyond.
She deserves it.
She's made this a must-be-at event. I'm guessing that's what brought Shira here.
Shira? Shira Huntzberger's here?
Rumsfeld, himself, would probably call her and thank her for the donation she made on the way in. Hillbilly Armor will be a thing of the past.
Where is she sitting?
Up front, table by the band.
Oh, my God.
What?
Oh, my God, excuse me.
Where's the seating chart?
What? Why?
There's been a terrible mistake.
What mistake?
You sat Shira Huntzberger at the slush table.
It was all that was available.
The slush table is the loser table.
But why would we have a loser table?
It's for people who show up unannounced.
She was unannounced.

Wow.

And Mitchum.

Paris?

You need Diazepam. 50, no,100 milligrams. I'll get my purse.

Well, the rich never are, because they don't have to be. When you control the means of production it reduces the incentive to humanize workers. Capitalist system--

The Patty Ballerinas, everybody.

Now, I would like to introduce a special new segment of my annual recital entitled "It was 20 years ago today." It's moments like these that make life worth living.
Ew.
Ew.
Ew!
Ew!
So, it's the birth of Lucille Ball?

He's moving along at a nice clip.

I'll catch you up when you return.

No, they weren't closed. I was... ...I don't know. It's... what it is. Nature.
Nature? Nature is...
You know, it's there I saw it, trees, leaves, whatever.
Okay. That's your second answer in the form of a haiku. Let's get beyond that. Why are you back?
Because I felt like coming back. I can't do what I wanna do?
Of course you can.
Good.
But camping is something you wanna do.
No, it's what you wanted me to do.
When did you turn against camping?
I didn't turn against camping. I'm just trying to understand why you were trying to get rid of me tonight.
I wasn't doing that.
You sent me off to the woods. What if I don't wanna go off to the woods?
You always wanna go to the woods.
I don't like going to the woods when I'm being banished to them.
No one is banishing you.
It felt like it.
Well, then, that's my fault.
Look. I like doing things with you. Surprised I have to tell you that.
You don't have to tell me that.

I like going shopping with you. I like having dinner with Sookie and Jackson. The actual shopping seems a little pointless and Sookie's kids drive me up a wall but you're there. And I like hanging with you.
I know that.
And I could have been fun at this recital. I mean, you're probably sitting there mocking most of it. I can mock stuff.
You're a great mocker. I was only thinking of you when I mentioned the camping. You haven't been camping since we got together and I was feeling weird about that. You should do the things you like.
I do do the things I like.

Well, I wasn't getting rid of you. I want you to do whatever you wanna do with me. I know that sounded dirty. And dirty things count. But I didn't mean the dirty things. You and me can hang whenever, wherever.
Yeah, well, maybe I'm being sensitive.
I really wasn't getting rid of you.
I mean, I'm not dying to see Baton Twirling.
I'm happy to be with a man who isn't.
Was there Baton Twirling?
Oh, yes. And it was no fun. She didn't drop it once.
You wanna come back to the recital with me? Kirk is doing something strange and disturbing.
No, I think I might go back out camping. Wouldn't mind doing some fishing.
Good.
Yeah.
Good.
Okay.
Excuse me. Thank you.
Hey.
Kirk's dying.
Oh.
Well, it's gonna happen to all of us one day.
Just not so spazzy.
Okay. Oh, wow!
Oh. You'd think they would have run out of glitter by now.
This is so stressful!
Richard.
Oh, Mitchum, old boy. I didn't know you were out there.
Just got here, it's quite the affair we got going here.
And for a wonderful cause.
Not stuffy like the others no smell of mothballs.
Well, you know my granddaughter is responsible for it.
Oh, yeah?
Planned the whole thing.
That's nice. I didn't know that. She's a sweet kid.
The sweetest.
Yeah. I wish Rory nothing but the best. I came straight from work without looking in a mirror. Wish I had.
Mitchum, just out of curiosity what happened with all of that?
All of what?
Uh that paper of yours in Stanford. Something, apparently, got blown out of proportion. There was some misunderstanding.
Oh, it was nothing much. She's a great kid.
She is. And a great journalist. I've read things she's written. She's a talent.
Maybe.
What do you mean "maybe"?
Well, I worked with her, Richard. I read her stuff too.
Meaning?
I've read great. I know what great is.
When I said great, I didn't mean she was Ben Bradley yet but she could be.
Anything's possible.
What exactly happened at that paper, Mitchum?
It didn't work out, Richard. It was just one of those things. She's better off for what I did.
And what exactly did you do?
Nothing you wouldn't have done.
Oh, and what was that?
You're in the business world. You have employees, yes?
Of course.
Say, you got a guy working in your office, you brought him in. Nice guy, everybody loves him but he just doesn't have it. He's a drain on the company. What are you gonna do?
My granddaughter was not a drain on your company.
My point is, that I wasn't going to put her in a position to become a drain. Now, Richard, really, we should get back out there.
What did you say to her?
Richard--
What did you say to her, Mitchum?
I did what I do with everyone. I called it like I saw it. I was honest with her. I don't pussyfoot. You know that.
You crushed her.
And if she's got what it takes, she'll bounce back. No one's ever criticized you, Richard reprimanded you, critiqued you? I find that hard to believe.
This is not about me.
She was in over her head. She lacked maturity.
She's not even 21!

Look, just blame me, okay? I felt bad that she had to sit through that disastrous dinner with Shira and pop going on about marriage and how she can't become a Huntzberger. I don't care about any of that. So, I gave her a shot, and she wasn't up to it.
You crushed that girl!
I did what I do.
We should have done this on the phone.
Richard, there you are! This is one of your favorites. And you're missing it.
It's all true, all of it.
What's true?
Everything she told us. Everything.
Everything who told us?
Lorelai... about what Mitchum did to Rory. How he said things to her, crushed her about Logan's whole family!
That can't be.
Mitchum just confirmed everything. He told that girl she wasn't good enough. I ought to punch him!
Richard. Calm down. People will hear.
They don't want her marrying into their precious family. They don't think she's good enough. He told her that she didn't have it. And you know she does! I know she does!
Of course, she does.
I can't stay in this room with these people.
Richard, go outside, get some air.
We should go home.
I'll catch up with you. Go outside.
Yeah, yeah.
Emily!

Oh, bless you, Emily. I'm undeserving.
Nonsense. It was a terrible mistake and it must be rectified.
Aren't they amazing? The whole combo is amazing. Follow me. Me, I love the Beatles. Mitchum took me to see Paul McCartney last year and I almost died. Come on.
So, Richard tells me we have a little problem.
Really? With what?
With the kids, Logan, Rory. I understand you're not exactly thrilled with the match that you let that be known to Rory at the dinner she had at your house.
Oh, well, I wouldn't say "not thrilled."
Then what would you say?
Oh, Emily, this is a party.
I'm just curious.
This may not be the time and place, Emily.
Let's make it the time and place.
Consider the discrepancies, Emily.
Well, that's what's confusing me. They both come from good families. They both have good values. Money doesn't seem to be an issue. We all have money.
Frankly, Emily, there's your money. Then there's our money.
Oh?
And our family has a lot of responsibilities that come with that, an image to maintain.

Ah, yes! Well, let me tell you this, Shira. We are just as good as you are. You don't think Rory is good enough for your son as if we don't know Logan's reputation we do. But he is welcome in our home anytime and you should extend the same courtesy to Rory.
Emily--

Let's talk about your money. You were a two-bit gold digger, fresh off the bus from Hicksville when you met Mitchum at whatever bar you happened to stumble into. Well, of course, you know. That would explain why your weight goes up and down 30 pounds every other month. But that's your cross to bear. But these are ugly realities. No one needs to talk about them. Those kids are staying together for as long as they like. You won't stop them. Now, enjoy the event.
Diane, hello.
The Swing Dolls, everybody.
I'm Rory Gilmore, the architect of this event.

Thank you and I'd like to take this moment to thank some others for the outstanding success this evening. To Lacey Boscombe, my right hand, my girl Friday. I could not have done it without you. Luke, hello? Luke! My door is chained! Especially funny, since I don't have a chain on my door. Luke!
Lorelai?
No. Land shark. Candy gram. Here's Johnny. Uh, Luke, open the door!
Stay there.

Aw, aw, I have a cramp. Luke, I have a cramp.
Sorry.

Alright, get your arm out of the way so I can unchain the door.
Sure, just yell, stand up already to the guy in the wheelchair.
I chained the door earlier to test it. Here.
Oh what an odd reward system you have.
Come with me.
What's going on?

Celebrating what?
Listen.
Are you cooking?
Is that listening?
Well, I'm hungry.
Focus.
I'm hungry.
Shh.
Fine.
I don't hear anything.
Exactly.
Okay, Simon, Garfunkel.
It's done.

The house. It's done.
No, it was supposed to take another week.

And he finished everything?
Yep! No more banging or sawing, no more paint cans lying around cigarette butts in the potted plants.
Well, they didn't put the light socket covers back on. They'll have to come back to put the light socket covers...
Light socket covers are on.
What about the skinny, tiny, molding in the closet? They have to fix the skinny, tiny molding in the closet.

Goodbye?

More pizza.

I gave them a going-away present. A $2,000 going-away present. That's gotta bring some smiles.

I am. I'm just sad at the same time. You've never been with a woman before?
Okay, fine. I've got another surprise for you.
What?
Upstairs.
Where?
Bedroom.
Upstairs in the bedroom? Whatever could it be?
Alright, close your eyes.
I'm not scared of it anymore, Luke.
Would you please just close your eyes?
Okay.
No, uh, uh. You ready?
Ready.
Take a look.
Wow! What is this?
This is my grandmother's bedroom set. It's in perfect shape. Can you imagine?
Oh, wow! Look at all the cherubs.
People have been trying to buy it off me for years but I always felt that I would eventually find the perfect place to put it, you know?
Uh-huh?
And then the room was done and just sittin' there and I remembered the day you came down to that storage unit and you saw the furniture, and you said you liked it.
I did?
Yeah and since you liked it and I've been looking for a place to put it, I figured--
When did I come to your storage unit?
Five years ago. You needed to borrow that space heater.
Oh, right.
And look, I haven't had a chance to put these up. Aren't they great?
Yes. Yes, they are.
You know, I was tempted to get them reframed but it just didn't seem right.
Oh, I-I've got one big eye. That's fun.
Yeah, that's the original glass. You can't find that anymore. So you sure you like it?
I love it.
Great. Okay. Well, let's get downstairs 'cause I am making risotto.
I just love it.
Sumatra, please get my granddaughter a plate.
That's alright, Sumatra. I'm just going up to my room.
Sumatra, please tell my granddaughter that all food is to be consumed in the dining room.
Sumatra, please tell my grandmother what?
That's the rule in this house, Rory.
I'm late for community service.
Food in this house is meant to be consumed in the dining room or not at all.
What about when you take your tea outside on the patio?
That is in the afternoon. This is morning. And in the morning you eat your food at the table in the dining room.
Fine. I'll be back this afternoon.
Well, if you expect that muffin to fly back to the kitchen you'd better go get it a cape.
Hey.
I have to go to China.
Enjoy your flight.
I need inspiration. I need ideas. I'm tapped out, boring. You know what's on the menu tonight?
What?
Goose with oyster stuffing.
What?
I know. But that's all I could come up with. And then, the only reason I thought of that was because Davey just learned "Duck, duck, goose" and the ducks looked puny, so there you go.
Well, say hi to Yao Ming for me.
Will do. What is this?
This is a formal invitation, written by me on the Dragonfly notepad about five minutes ago inviting you and Jackson to a house-warming dinner at my newly completed pad.
It's done.
It's done. Saturday night. I've heard it's alright for fighting get a little action in.
Wow. Your house is done. This is so exciting! How does it look?
It uh, looks great.
It, uh, does?
Yeah.
Why do you hate it?

I don't hate it. It's-it's beautiful. It's just, okay, what if Jackson brought home a set of his grandmother's pots and pans? Do the cherubs interfere with the actual cooking function or are they just decorative?

What happened to my old pots and pans?

Can I get them back?
Babette's nephew, Gary, is sleeping on them.
Sleeping on them?

Well, what are you talking about?
I am talking about Luke's grandmother's bedroom furniture that he set up in my brand new bedroom.
Oh.
And he loves this furniture.
And you don't?
No, I don't. But it shouldn't matter, right?
Why not?

Look at everything Luke has done for me. I mean, he bought the Twickham House and then he unbought the Twickham House and then he almost bought it again and then he decided to live at my house because I wanted to live at my house.
Yeah, he did.
He has turned his whole life upside down for me. He does everything in his power to make me happy and give me what I want so can't I give him this one little thing?
Yes, you can.

No, I can't. The bed is small and really low just perfect for tiny, shrunken limbs that can't be too far off the ground. And then he has this ancient dresser with the original funhouse mirror in it so that when I wake up every morning and I am at my most visually vulnerable I'll look in there and-and think I'm that kid from "Mask."
You can replace the mirror.
Oh no. He loves the mirror and the bed and the dresser. Oh, and did I tell you about the paintings?
No.
Of sailboats?
Oh.
There's six of them. Six sailboats waiting to sail me away to an old folks home and then, when the wind's right drop me off at the Pearly Gates. I'm hateful and selfish.
No, you're not.

I just want my new house to be perfect. Half that crap in there was hand-me-downs to begin with. You know, I had that old bed that Mia let me snag from the independence inn. Just wanted something new.
You have to tell him.
I can't tell him.
Maybe it's not so bad.
Well, you'll see for yourself on Saturday night, 7:30?
Aye, aye, captain.
Hmm.
Emily, sorry to be so late. Jenson wouldn't stop talking.

The car will be here in 20 minutes to take me to the airport. Remember, I'm not gonna be back until Tuesday so you're going to have to deal with Alejandro yourself. I will leave you the check. Your safe return, darling, is all I need.
Who the hell are you?
Well, if I knew that, I could dismiss my therapist, couldn't I? Though she's very hot.
I'm Colin McCrae.
How wonderful for you. What are you doing in my house? Put that box down. Both of you, explain yourselves.
Mr. Gilmore, I'm Colin McCrae. You know my father, Andrew McCrae.
Yes, I know Andrew McCrae. What are you doing in my house? Where's Mrs. Gilmore?
Don't know, mate. Rory let us in.
We came over to help her move her stuff.
Move her stuff where?
To her new place of residence.
What do you mean? New place of residence? Rory's moving out?
I hope so. Otherwise, she'll have nothing to wear tomorrow.
Well, that's preposterous! A person doesn't just move out without a word. Where is she? Rory!
She already left.
Well, I want an explanation.
We'll have her call you.
You, you're... Well, what are you doing with that? That's my tennis racket.
I told you she didn't point to the closet on the right.
Well, then, I have no idea what closet she was pointing to.
I suppose these humidors aren't hers, either. Pity. Any chance you're sick of them? I promise to give them a nice home and show them a picture of you every year at Christmas.
Very tall man, that one.
They're gonna get cold.
Are they different?
Different than what?
They seem different.
They're nachos. Now eat them.
You used baked chips.
What?
You did, didn't you? You used baked chips and low-fat cheese.
I did not use low-fat cheese--
Ha!
How can you tell?
How could you lie?
They taste the same!
Oh, the trust, Luke. How are we gonna to make it if you're constantly trying to keep me healthy?
Fine, forget it. Die at 60.
Bring me a doughnut while I wait. Hey, Lane. Yoo-hoo! Lane! Whoa! Lane, seriously. I'm landing planes over here.
Lorelai! Hey.
Hey, fill me up here.
So, how's it going?
Good.
Good. I haven't seen you in the last couple days.
I've been working the lunch shift.
Oh. Something wrong?
Wrong?
Yeah, you're-you're giving me a-a Valerie Cherish, you know and I don't wanna see that.
It's a great show. You should watch it.
I will.
It's cancelled.
Oh, sorry.
Well, it's your fault, so...

Wow, what's going on here? Usually when I come in, you say hi and then I say hi and you tell me what's going on in your life and I tell you what's going on in my life. It's not curing the bird flu or anything but it's been a nice tradition.
Rory moved in with me.
She... But why? What happened?
I don't really know. We haven't had the in depth conversation yet. She just said she moved out of her grandparents' house and needed a place to crash.
Wow, that's pretty big.
Yeah. And she didn't tell me if I could say anything to you. So I just assumed I shouldn't.
Right, I get it. I heard nothing.
So it's nice of you to let her crash.
Hey she's small. How much room can she take up, right?
Did she bring her books?
Good point.
Are you okay?
Me? Sure. I'm fine. A little curious, but I'm fine.
Well, when I know more...
Right.
Okay.
Okay.
Okay.
Okay.
Lunch is served.
Such service.
I'm just in it for the tips.
Underwear first, then pants.
What a shame? I'm away from my snare drum.
You want a soda?
Please, soda me.
Shampoo's looking low.
I'll get more tomorrow.
Four people in the house sure makes the shampoo go away faster, huh?
I brought my own shampoo, Zach.
Hey, not a judgment, just an observation. Two paper towels, huh?
Relax, Zach.
Hey, it's cool. Just paper towels don't grow on trees. They cost money. Use two a day for a month, that's like 60 paper towels. You're looking at 24 rolls per year.
I'm not staying that long, Zach.
Hey, Lane's casa es su casa, apparently. Oh, cool! Don't have to strain myself by lifting a full box. Excellent.
I'm not staying that long, Zach.
She's not staying that long, Zach. A couple of days, tops.

Yeah? Remember Don? He came for a couple days, tops, once. Six weeks later, he's still here. Ate all my cheese nips, but when I confronted him with the box he said they were just settling. Dude had cheese nip breath as he told me they were just settling.
Oh my God, Zach, I am not staying that long. Hello.
Rory Gilmore, please.
This is Rory Gilmore.
Rory, this is Stuart Wultz of the Stamford Eagle-Gazette.
Mr. Wultz, yes. Um, thank you so much for calling me back.
No problem. Listen, I got your message and of course I'll be happy to give you a reference. I'll even make it a great one.
Really?
Look, I don't really know what happened with you and Mitchum but from me to you, you're a sharp kid and you got a lot going for you. Anybody would be lucky to have you working for them.
Thank you so much.
I know this'll shock you but you're not the first person who couldn't get along with Herr Huntzberger. It's a pretty big club, actually. Ignore him.
I plan on doing just that.
Good. Okay, so, just, uh, have whoever you want call me and I'll sing your praises. Sorry I can't hire you at The Gazette but we don't have any openings right now anyhow, so...
That's okay. The reference will be plenty.
Good luck, Rory. I expect to hear great things about you someday.
I promise not to let you down. Goodbye, Mr. Wultz. Yes!
Good news?
References are now officially in order which is a relief because I've already sent out a 125,000 resumes.
Oh, listen, I forgot to tell you. I may have done something stupid.
What?
Well, I kind of told Lorelai that you moved in here.
I'm sorry? Moved in here?
Zach, there must be something else you can do.
When did you see my mom?
This morning at Luke's. I'm sorry. I didn't know what to say. I didn't know if you wanted her to know or didn't want her to know.
It's okay, it's fine that she knows.
Oh, good.
Okay, it's time to get dressed and hit the pavement.
Wait. Your sandwich.
Thank you.

Zach.
What? I'm just writing a song.

What are you talking about? Look at the brand new napkin holder. It used to be a cow. Now it's a much bigger cow.
Fine. Forget it. Chicken and dumplings going in.

Look, if by some chance Luke happens to burn the chicken or overcook the burgers, then we won't starve. If everything turns out perfect then you can freeze the casserole and eat it for the rest of your life.
Perfect plan.
Forget it.
There is no shame in using a charcoal chimney.
It's a gadget. I don't do gadgets.
It takes twice as long.
You got some place to be?
No, you just go right ahead and rub those sticks together. I'll just go learn a language or something.
Bernardo. Riff.
And a real man doesn't use a charcoal chimney.

He is too. I have pictures to prove it.
Do you have a spray bottle?
For what?
To spray the flames down if they get too high. Or do you just use a hose?

And then he challenges them to an arm-wrestling contest.

Okay, boys are busy. The chicken's in the oven. Show me the bedroom set.
Sookie.
I want to see the creepy granny bed.
Oh, I'm trying to rise above it.
Rise above it later. Let's go.
Here it is.
Huh.
It's terrible, right?
Well, it's...
Terrible?
Really terrible.
I told you.
Aw. Oh, my God. You can't sleep in this.
Don't worry, I won't. I'm convinced it's haunted and one night Luke will come back from the bathroom and find nothing but a bloody hook hanging from the cherubs.
Oh my god. I just saw the cherubs. Okay, let's think. Maybe if you stripped the wood--
And lit a match?
Throw on a little gasoline.
I can't tell him I hate it.
Yeah, you have to. It's horrible.
Yes, but Luke loves this furniture.
Right. Luke loves this furniture. Luke loves this furniture. Luke loves this furniture?
Yes.
Has he seen it? Has he seen this? And that, has he seen that?
Come on.
Oh, now, I know he hasn't seen that.
I'm going to check on the chicken.
Hey, Lore. Haven't said that in a while.
Is that...
Uh, anyway. I hope you're good. Hope Rory is good. I wanted to talk to you, nothing terrifying. I think I have good news. In fact, I know I have good news. Anyhow I'm hoping you'll call me back and--
Hey. How's the food coming? I'm starving. Who was that? It sounded like Christopher.
Bye-bye.
Well, if you knew who it was, why'd you ask?
Were you gonna tell me he called?
Luke, yes.
Well, then, why'd you turn the machine off when I walked in?
It-It was a reflex.
Reflex?

How long has this been going on?

Last time we were over Sookie breast fed Martha during appetizers, we owe them.
I won't discuss this with people in the house, it's rude.
No it's rude to silently sulk through dinner and make them feel incredibly uncomfortable because they know we're fighting and we're pretending we're not fighting.
We're not fighting... ...yet.
So we're standing in a giant pile of manure and I am screaming, "I asked for extra fish heads!" And he's like, "No, you did not ask for extra fish heads." Oh, I tell you, it was hilarious.

The chicken and dumplings are good too.

People in Kansas talk funny.

Oh, yes, it is. It is not lost on me that the burgers with my world famous rub are almost gone, while your butter burgers are still sitting there on the plate. You a little humbled now, my friend?
Jackson.
My burgers are better. Admit it. I demand satisfaction.

Hey.

I can admit it. I have no trouble telling someone something no matter how uncomfortable it might make them.

Lorelai and Luke are fighting.
We're not fighting.

It's rude.
Now, we wouldn't wanna be rude.
It's fine. Just eat. What's that?
Chicken and dumplings?
Who the hell made chicken and dumplings?
Sookie, our guest, who we don't want to be rude to.
I'm not the one who started this.
Uh, I'm sorry. Are we talking about this now?
You knew how I'd feel about it.
And you have absolutely no reason to be upset.
Oh I don't? You were hiding--

You hung up the phone just as I came--
You didn't let me explain. I was about to tell you.
At that moment, it was not appropriate to talk about it--
So you'd rather just sit and stew and be mad for no reason?

In a year, Luke! The last time I saw him was the last time you saw him!
Well, I don't believe in coincidences.
This is not fair!
I have a right to expect a little honesty from my fiancee!
Okay, you want honesty? I'll give you honesty. I hate that bedroom set. It's old and creepy and I hate it.
You told me you loved it.
I have absolutely no memory of coming to your storage unit five years ago and telling you I love that furniture.
Well, Thank you very much for your honesty about my grandmother's furniture. Too bad you're not more forthcoming about the other men in your life.
Oh, my God. Enjoy Wisteria Lane. You major drama queen.
I'm done.
Wrap yourself in a towel and trip over a hedge on your way out!
Are you okay?
Yeah, I'm fine. I'm sorry, you guys. Give Paul Anka the burger.
Was it because I brought up my meat rub?
Yes, it was.
Come in.

When we're married, huh? Gee, when's that gonna be?
I brought you something to eat. You're gonna need sustenance if we're gonna go another 10 rounds.
I'm never gonna be okay with Christopher being in your life.
I'm always going to have Christopher in my life.
Yeah.

Today was the first day I heard Christopher's voice in a year and I would have told you.
We can't hide things from each other.
I know.

Agreed.

I think they enjoyed watching a show for once that didn't have lala playing the guitar.
Come here.
I want a Barbie and a pony and roller skates and roller skates for the Barbie and for the pony.

Cross my heart and hope to die.

No secrets.
Luke.
Yeah?

Shh.
Stamford Eagle-Gazette. I'll transfer you. Stamford Eagle-Gazette. I'll transfer you. Stamford Eagle-Gazette. I'll transfer you. Stamford Eagle-Gazette. I'll transfer you.

Rory Gilmore.
As you live and breathe.

Okay, I think maybe we got our signals crossed earlier. I thought I was clear. I don't have any jobs.
No, you were very clear. You said you didn't have any jobs available, and I heard you. I have excellent hearing, among my many other qualifications which I have listed here on my resume.
Your...

If I gave you a job, I'd have to fire Harry.
Five minutes.
Sorry.

Steaks and eggs. Tuna melt.

No.

Oh, boy.
You know where to find me.
More books.

Did you call her cell?

Mom.

Mom I've never thought that--

No--

Mom.

And you didn't lose me.

Anna?

Oh. Here.

episodes.title: New and Improved Lorelai
episodes.summary: Luke responds to Lorelai. Rory faces legal consequences. Angry with Rory, Richard and Emily, Lorelai cuts off ties with them.

episodes.title: Fight Face
episodes.summary: Rory winds up in a fight while performing community service. Lorelai gets a dog. Luke and Lorelai decide to renovate Lorelai's house.

episodes.title: The UnGraduate
episodes.summary: Rory takes a job at Emily's Daughters of the American Revolution office and serves as her grandmother's spy. Lorelai won't commit to a date.

episodes.title: Always a Godmother, Never a God
episodes.summary: Sookie hopes to reconcile the estranged Gilmore girls by asking both Lorelai and Rory to be godparents to her kids, but things don't go as planned.

episodes.title: We've Got Magic to Do
episodes.summary: After two separate confrontations with the Huntzbergers at a D.A.R. party, Richard and Emily realize Lorelai was right about their treatment of Rory.

episodes.title: Welcome to the Doll House
episodes.summary: After asking Logan about Rory's future plans, Richard admits it was a mistake to let Rory make rash decisions and discusses the matter with Lorelai.

episodes.title: Twenty-One is the Loneliest Number
episodes.summary: Both Lorelai and Rory are saddened that their estrangement will keep them from spending Rory's 21st birthday the way they had always planned.

episodes.title: Let Me Hear Your Balalaikas Ringing Out
episodes.summary: When her former boyfriend visits and reveals an amazing success, Rory begins rethinking the choices she's made with her life.

episodes.title: The Prodigal Daughter Returns
episodes.summary: After months of estrangement, Lorelai and Rory make their first move toward reconciliation. Luke gets a big surprise but conceals it from Lorelai.

episodes.title: He's Slippin’ ‘Em Bread... Dig?
episodes.summary: Rory's long-absent father reappears in her and Lorelai's lives, casting uncertainty on what this will mean for Lorelai's current relationship.

episodes.title: The Perfect Dress
episodes.summary: Wanting to get to know his newly discovered relative, Luke makes a visit. Lorelai sets a date but has a feeling something's not right.

episodes.title: Just Like Gwen and Gavin
episodes.summary: Lorelai finds out about Luke's secret, but not from Luke. She tries to be supportive, but Luke's reaction hurts her. Logan tries to win over Rory.

episodes.title: Friday Night's Alright for Fighting
episodes.summary: Luke gets to know April. Rory tries to get the school newspaper published after the staff quits. All four Gilmores vent their frustrations.

episodes.title: You've Been Gilmored
episodes.summary: Lorelai brings Luke to dinner with her parents. When Rory becomes the new editor of the school paper, her roommate kicks her out of their apartment.

episodes.title: A Vineyard Valentine
episodes.summary: Rory, Lorelai and their beaus spend Valentine's Day weekend on Martha's Vineyard. During their stay, Rory's boyfriend saves the day.

episodes.title: Bridesmaids Revisited
episodes.summary: Rory dazzles the crowd at a journalism panel, but the next day, she's devastated to learn how her boyfriend behaved during their breakup.

episodes.title: I'm OK, You're OK
episodes.summary: Rory forgives her beau. Luke's girlfriend is secretly upset when he spends a few days with April. Rory does some spying on her mother's behalf.

episodes.title: The Real Paul Anka
episodes.summary: Unhappy because Rory hasn't really forgiven him, Logan takes off with his friends. Rory runs into Luke and April at a bookstore in Philadelphia.

episodes.title: I Get A Sidekick Out of You
episodes.summary: After she and her mother scramble to accommodate an unexpected visitor, Lane takes a big step in her life. Lorelai gives in to self-pity.

episodes.title: Super Cool Party People
episodes.summary: When Luke plans a birthday party for April at the diner, Lorelai wants to help and is hurt that Luke thinks it's too soon for her to meet April.

episodes.title: Driving Miss Gilmore
